what_its_for: PEG-3350 is a laxative used to treat occasional constipation. It works by drawing water into your colon, which softens your stool and makes it easier to pass. It is not a stimulant laxative, so it works gently without causing cramping in most people.
how_to_take: Mix one dose (one capful or 17 grams) into 4 to 8 ounces (about half a cup to a full cup) of any beverage you enjoy, such as water, juice, coffee, or tea. Stir well until the powder is completely dissolved — it should be clear and you should not see any powder. Then drink the entire mixture. You can take it at any time of day, with or without food. Use the measuring cap that comes with the bottle to make sure you get the right amount each time.
dosing: Adults and children 17 years and older: Take one dose (17 grams, which is one capful) by mouth once a day. Do not take more than one dose per day. Do not use this medicine for more than 7 days in a row unless your doctor tells you to. Your doctor may give you different instructions, so always follow what your doctor says. For children under 17 years of age, check with your child's doctor before using.
missed_dose: If you forget to take your dose, just take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up by taking two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not take more than the recommended dose per day. Do not use it for longer than 7 days without talking to your doctor first. Avoid using other laxatives at the same time unless your doctor tells you to. If you have been told to limit your fluid intake for any medical reason, talk to your doctor before using this product, since you need to drink it with a full beverage.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe stomach pain or cramping, nausea or vomiting that does not go away, blood in your stool, no bowel movement after 7 days of use, a sudden change in your bowel habits that has lasted more than 2 weeks, signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you have rectal bleeding or if constipation continues after using this medicine.
when_it_works: PEG-3350 usually produces a bowel movement within 1 to 3 days of starting treatment. It does not work immediately like some other laxatives. If you do not have a bowel movement after 3 days of use, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using PEG-3350 if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children under 17 years old: Always check with your child's pediatrician before giving this medicine to a child, as dosing is different for younger children. Older adults: PEG-3350 is generally safe for older adults, but make sure to stay well hydrated. People with kidney disease, heart disease, or those on a special fluid-restricted diet should speak with their doctor before using this product.
